translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy the brother, to the churches of God which are in Corinth, together with all the saints who are in all Achaia.
Grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed is God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort,
who comforts us in all our afflictions, so that we too may be able to comfort all those who are afflicted with that comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
For just as the sufferings of Christ abound toward us, so also through Christ our comforts abound.
If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation, which is brought about by enduring those sufferings that we also suffer. And our hope for you is firm.
You know that just as you share in those sufferings, so also you share in the comfort.
For I do not want you, brothers, to be ignorant about our affliction which befell us in Asia; for it weighed upon us exceedingly, beyond our strength, so that we even despaired of life itself.
But we ourselves received in ourselves the sentence of death, so that we should not trust in ourselves but in God, who raises the dead,
who delivered us from such a death and will deliver us, in whom we hope that he will deliver us yet again,
through the help of your prayers for us, so that thanks may be given by many on our behalf for the gift granted to us through many persons.

For this is our boast, the testimony of our conscience: that in holiness and godly truth, not by fleshly wisdom but by the grace of God, we have conducted ourselves in the world, and all the more toward you.
For we write nothing else to you than what you read and have come to know; and I hope that you will understand fully,
just as you have come to know us in part, that we are your boast, as you also are ours, on the day of the Lord Jesus.
And with this same confidence I wanted to come to you first, so that you might have a second joy,
and to pass through you into Macedonia, and to come back to you again from Macedonia, and to be sent on by you to Judea.
When I planned this, did I perhaps act lightly in some way? Or what I plan, do I plan in a fleshly way, so that with me there should be "yes, yes" and "no, no"?
But God is faithful, for our word to you is not "yes" and "no."
For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, by me and by Silvanus and by Timothy, was not "yes" and "no"; rather, in him it has become "yes."
For however many are the promises of God, in him is the "yes," and through us the "amen," to the glory of God.
Now the one who establishes us with you in Christ and has anointed us is God,
who has also sealed us and given the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts.
But I call upon God as witness against my soul that it was to spare you that I did not come again to Corinth.
Not that we have any lordship over that faith of yours; rather, we are helpers of your joy, for you stand firm by faith.
And I resolved this in my own heart, that I would not come to you again in sorrow.
For if I grieve you, then who is there to gladden me, if not the one who has been grieved by me?
And I wrote this very thing to you so that, when I come, sorrow would not be added to sorrow from those from whom I ought to have joy. I trust in all of you, that my joy is the joy of you all.
For I wrote to you out of much affliction and anguish of heart, with many tears, not so that you would be grieved, but so that you would know the love that I have, all the more, toward you.
If anyone has grieved me, he has not grieved me, but in some part (so that I do not burden you) all of you.
This rebuke from the many is enough for such a person.
So now, on the contrary, you should rather forgive him and comfort him, or such a person may be swallowed up by too much sorrow.
Therefore I beseech you to confirm your love toward him.
For this is also why I wrote, so that I might know your proven character, whether you are obedient in everything.
And whatever you forgive, I forgive too. For whatever I have forgiven, I have forgiven for your sake in the presence of Christ,
so that we may not be taken advantage of by the devil, for we are not ignorant of his designs.
Now when I came to Troas for the gospel of Christ, and a great door had been opened to me by the Lord,
I had no rest in my spirit, because I did not find Titus, my brother. So I took leave of them and went out to Macedonia.
But thanks be to God, who always spreads us forth [?] through Christ, and through us makes the odor of fragrance known in every place.
For we are the fragrance of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing:
to some an odor from death to death, and to others an odor from life to life. And who is sufficient for this?
For we are not like the many who peddle the word of God. Rather, we speak from truth, as from God, before God, in Christ.
Am I beginning to commend ourselves again? Do we need anything, as some do, a letter of commendation to you or from you?
But you are our letter from the Lord, written on our hearts, known and read by all people.

It is clear that you are an apostolic letter of Christ, ministered by us. It is written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on fleshly tablets of the heart.
Such is the hope we have through Christ toward God.
Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to count anything as coming from us; rather, our sufficiency is from God,
who has made us sufficient to be ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

If the ministry of death, engraved in letters on tablets, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not fix their eyes on the face of Moses because of the glory of his face, a glory that was passing away,
How much more will the ministry of the Spirit be in glory?
If the ministry of condemnation was in glory, how much more will the ministry of the Spirit surpass it in glory.
For indeed, what was glorified is no longer glorified in this respect, because of the glory that surpasses it.
If what was passing away came with glory, how much more will what remains be in glory.
Since we have such a hope, let us act with great openness,
and not like Moses, who put a veil over his face so that the children of Israel would not see the end of what was passing away.
But their minds were blinded. To this very day the same veil remains at the reading of the old law and has not been taken off, because it is done away with through Christ.
To this very day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart.
But when one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
And we, with unveiled face, behold the glory of the Lord and are changed into that same image, from glory to glory, as from the Lord, the Spirit.
Therefore, since we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, let us not lose heart,
but let us renounce the hidden things of shame. For we do not walk in craftiness, nor do we falsify the word of God, but by making the truth plain we commend ourselves to every human mind before God.
If this gospel of ours is hidden, it is hidden among those who are perishing,
the unbelievers, whose minds the god of this world has blinded, so that the light of the glory of Christ, who is the image of the invisible God, may not shine on them.
For we do not preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Christ's sake.
God, who said that light should shine forth, is the one who has shone in our hearts to enlighten us with the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
We have this treasure in earthen vessels, so that the surpassing greatness of the power may be God's and not from us.
We are afflicted in every way, but not crushed; though we are at a loss, we are not given up to despair;
though we are persecuted, we are not forsaken; though we are struck down, we are not destroyed.
We always carry the death of Christ in our bodies, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our bodies.
For we who live are always being handed over to death for Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in these mortal bodies of ours.
So from now on death is at work in us, but life among you.
We have the same spirit of faith, as it is written: "I believed what I was speaking." We also believe, and for that reason we speak.
We know this: the one who raised the Lord Jesus from the dead will also raise us with Jesus and present us together with you.
For all things are for your sake, so that the grace may abound through the many, and the thanksgiving may overflow to the glory of God.
Therefore I do not lose heart. Even though this outer self of ours is wasting away, our inner self is being renewed day by day.
For this brief, slight affliction of ours is producing for us a surpassing, great glory.
For we do not look for what is visible but for what is invisible. What is visible is temporary, but what is invisible is eternal.
We know this: if this earthly house, our dwelling, is torn down, we have a house built by God, not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
And because of this we groan, and we long to put on our dwelling from heaven,
so that even if we have been stripped, we will not be found naked.
And we who are still in this dwelling groan and are weighed down, because we do not wish to be stripped but to be clothed, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
But the one who works this in us is God, who has given us the pledge of the Spirit.
So we are always confident, and we know that we have come into this flesh and have gone away from the Lord.
We walk by faith and not by doubt.
We are confident, and we would rather leave the flesh and go to the Lord.
For this reason we are also honoured, so that whether we come in or go out, we may be pleasing to him.
For all of us must be made manifest before the judgement seats of Christ, so that each one may receive for what he has done in the body, whether good or evil.
Now, since we know the fear of God, do we persuade people? But we are manifest before God, and we trust that we are also manifest in your minds.
We are not commending ourselves to you again. Instead we are giving you reason to boast about us, so that you may have something to say to those who boast only in appearance and not in heart.
If we have been out of our minds, it is for God; or if we make you wise, it is for you.
For the love of Christ compels us to judge this: that one died for all, so then did all die?
And he died for all, so that those who live might no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for them and rose again.
From now on we know no one according to the flesh. Even if we once knew Christ according to the flesh, now we no longer know him in that way.
From now on, whatever is in Christ is a new creation. The old has passed away, and behold, the new has now come into being.
And all things are from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
For God was with Christ, reconciling the world to himself, not counting their sins against them, and he entrusted to us the word of reconciliation.
We are ambassadors for Christ, as God appeals through us. We implore you for Christ's sake: be reconciled to God.
For the one who knew no sin he made to be sin for our sake, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
We are your helpers, and we beg you: do not let the grace of God you have received go for nothing.
For he says: "At the time of acceptance I listened to you, and on the day of salvation I helped you." Brothers, see, now is the time of acceptance; now is the day of salvation.
Do not put a stumbling block in anyone's way in anything, so that the ministry is not blamed.
Instead, in everything present yourselves as servants of God: through great endurance, in afflictions and sorrows, in hardships,
in beatings, in imprisonments, in riots, in labours, in sleepless nights, in fasting,
by purity, by knowledge, by patience, by kindness, by the Holy Spirit, by sincere love,
by the word of truth, by the power of God, with the weapons of righteousness for the right hand and for the left,
through honour and dishonour, through slander and praise; treated as deceivers, and yet true;
as unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and see, we are alive; as punished, and yet not put to death;
as sorrowful, and yet we always rejoice; as poor, and yet we make many rich; as having nothing, and yet we have everything.
Corinthians, we have spoken openly to you, and our heart is opened wide.
You are not restricted by us; you are restricted by your own hearts.
In return, the same in exchange (I speak as to children): you too open wide your hearts.
Do not be yoked together with unbelievers. What partnership is there between righteousness and lawlessness? Or what fellowship is there between light and darkness?
Or what agreement does Christ have with Belial? Or what share does a believer have with an unbeliever?

Or what agreement can the temple of God have with idols? For we are temples of the living God, as God said: "I will dwell among them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be my people."
"Therefore come out from among them and be separate," says the Lord, "and do not touch what is unclean, and I will welcome you."
"And I will be a Father to you, and you will be my sons and daughters," says the Lord Almighty.
Therefore, beloved, since I have this promise, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, and make our holiness complete in the fear of God.
Forgive us: we have wronged no one, we have angered no one, we have cheated no one.
I do not say this to condemn you. I said before that you are in our hearts, so that we die together and live together.
I have great confidence in you; I have great pride in you. I am filled with comfort; I overflow with joy in all our afflictions.
When we came into Macedonia, our bodies had no relief at all. We were afflicted in every way: fighting outside, fears inside.
But God, who comforts the lowly, comforted us by the arrival of Titus,
and not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort he had received from you. He told us about your longing, your eagerness and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced still more.
Even if I grieved you with that letter, I do not regret it, though I did regret it; for I see that the letter grieved you, if only for a while.
Now I rejoice, not because you were grieved, but because you were grieved into repentance. For you were grieved for God's sake, so that you suffered no loss through us.
For grief that comes from God brings about a repentance that leads to life and is not to be regretted, but the grief of this world brings about death.

For see how much eagerness this very grief of yours, which is from God, has produced among you: how much clearing of yourselves, or how much relief, or how much fear, how much longing, how much zeal, or how much punishment of wrong! In everything you have shown yourselves to be pure in that matter.
So even though I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of the one who did the wrong, nor for the sake of the one who was wronged, but so that your eagerness toward us might be made known before God.
Therefore we have been comforted in our comfort. And we rejoiced even more, far more, at the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
For whatever I boasted to him about you, I was not put to shame. Just as everything I told you was true, so our boasting to Titus has also proved true.
And his compassion toward you is all the greater as he remembers the obedience of all of you, and how you received him with fear and trembling.
I rejoice that in everything we can be confident about you.
Brothers, I want you to know about the grace of God that has been given to the churches of Macedonia.
For in a great testing by affliction, their overflowing joy and their deep poverty have overflowed into a wealth of generosity on their part.
For I bear witness that they gave as much as they were able, and even beyond what they were able, of their own free will.
With much pleading they begged us for the favor of taking part in the service to the saints.
And they did not do only what we had hoped. They first gave themselves to the Lord, and then to us, by the will of God.
So we urged Titus that, just as he had begun this beforehand, he should also complete this grace among you.
But just as you excel in everything (in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in all eagerness, and in the love from us that is among you), see that you also excel in this grace.
I am not saying this as a command. Rather, by means of the eagerness of others I am testing whether your love is sincere.
For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ: though he was rich, he became poor for your sake, so that through his poverty you might become rich.
And in this I give you my advice, for this is better for you. Last year you were the first to begin, not only in doing but also in wanting to do.
But now finish the doing as well, so that your eagerness to want it may be matched by your completing it out of what you have.
For if the eagerness is there, the gift is acceptable according to what a person has, not according to what he does not have.
It is not that others should have ease and you hardship, but that there should be equality.
At the present time your abundance should supply what they lack, so that their abundance may also supply what you lack, and so there may be equality.
As it is written: "The one who gathered much did not have too much, and the one who gathered little did not have too little."
But thanks be to God, who put the same zeal into the heart of Titus for you.
For he accepted our request, and being all the more zealous, he went out to you of his own accord.
And we have sent with him the brother whose praise in the gospel is spread through all the churches.

Not only that, but he was also blessed by the churches with the laying on of hands as our fellow traveller in this gift of grace, which we are administering for the glory of the Lord himself and because of your eagerness.
We are taking care about this, so that no one may blame us over this generous gift that we are administering.
For we plan in advance what is good, not only before the Lord but also before people.
And with them we have sent our brother, whom we have often tested in many matters and found zealous. Now he is even more zealous because of his great confidence in you.
As for Titus, he is my partner in the work and a helper for you. As for our brothers, they are apostles of the churches and the glory of Christ.
So show them, before the churches, the proof of your love and of our boasting about you.
Now concerning the ministry to the saints, there is no need for me to write to you.
For I know your eagerness toward us. I boasted about it to the Macedonians, telling them that Achaia has been ready since last year, and your zeal has stirred up many.
I have sent the brothers so that our boasting about you may not prove empty in this matter, and so that you may be ready, as we have been saying.
Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we would be put to shame in this matter, not to mention you.

So I thought it better to ask the brothers to go to you ahead of time and arrange in advance the gift of blessing you promised earlier. That way it will be ready as a blessing and not as something extorted.
Remember this: whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows with blessing will also reap with blessing.
Each person should give as they have decided in their heart, not with sorrow and not unwillingly, for God loves what is given cheerfully.
And God is able to give you more than enough of everything you need, so that in every way and at all times you may have everything without lack, and may abound in every good work.
As it is written: "He scattered abroad and gave to the poor; his righteousness endures forever."
May the one who gives seed to the sower and bread for food give to you as well. May he multiply your seed and increase the fruit of your righteousness.
May he make you rich in every way for all kinds of generosity, which through us produces thanksgiving to God.
For the ministry of this offering does more than supply what the saints lack. It also overflows through many in thanksgiving to God.
Through the proof that this ministry gives, you glorify God by the obedience of your confession to the gospel of Christ and by the generosity of your sharing with them and with everyone.
And in their prayer for you, they long for you because of the surpassing grace of God that is upon you.
Thanks be to God for his indescribable gifts.
I, Paul, entreat you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ: I who am lowly among you when face to face, but am bold toward you when absent.
But I entreat you that I may not have to be bold when face to face with the confidence with which I think to be bold against those who regard us as walking according to the flesh.
For though we still live in the flesh, we are not arrayed for battle according to the flesh,
for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but mighty through God for pulling down strongholds. We pull down the reasonings of the heart
and every height that is raised up against the knowledge of God, and we take captive every thought into obedience to Christ,
and we hold ourselves ready to punish all disobedience when your obedience is complete.
You look at each person's outward appearance. If anyone trusts that he himself belongs to Christ, let him consider this again within himself: that just as he belongs to Christ, so do we.
For even if I should boast somewhat more about this authority of ours, which the Lord gave us for building you up and not for tearing you down, I would not be put to shame,
so that you may not think that I am trying to frighten you with these letters.
For, as it were, "these letters are weighty and strong, but his coming in bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible."
Let such a person consider this again: that what we are in word through letters when absent, we are also in deed when present.
For we do not dare to judge or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves. But they measure themselves by themselves and commend themselves, and they themselves do not understand themselves.
But we will not boast beyond measure, but according to the measure of the rule that God has allotted to us, a measure reaching even as far as you.
For we are not overextending ourselves, as though we did not reach as far as you, for we came even as far as you with the gospel of Christ.
We do not boast beyond measure in another's labors, but we have hope that, as your faith grows, we will be enlarged among you still more, according to our rule,
so as to preach the gospel in the regions beyond you, not boasting in what has been made ready within another's rule.
But let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.
For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
Would that you might bear with me in a little foolishness of mine; but indeed, do bear with me,
for I am jealous over you with the jealousy of God, for I betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
But I am afraid that, just as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, so your minds may be corrupted from simplicity toward Christ.

For if someone comes and preaches another Jesus whom we did not preach, or if he brings another spirit which you did not receive, or another gospel which you did not accept, you do well indeed [to bear with it].
For I think that I am in no way inferior to those super-apostles.
And even if I am unskilled in speech, I am not so in knowledge; rather, in every way we have made this plain to you in all things.
Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I preached the word of God to you free of charge?
I plundered other churches and took provisions so that I could serve you. And when I came to you and was in need, I did not burden any of you.
For the brothers who came from Macedonia filled up what I lacked. In everything I kept myself from being a burden to you, and I will keep doing so.
The truth of Christ is in me: this boasting of mine will not be stopped in the regions of Achaia.
Why? Because I do not love you? God knows this.
But I am doing this, and I will keep doing it, so that I may cut off the opportunity from those who want an opportunity, so that in what they boast of they may be found just as we are.
For such people are false apostles, deceitful workers, who disguise themselves as apostles of Christ.
And it is no wonder, for the devil himself disguises himself as an angel of light.
So it is no great thing if his servants also disguise themselves as servants of righteousness. Their end will be according to their deeds.
I say again: let no one think me foolish. But if you do, then at least bear with me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
What I am saying, I do not say according to the Lord, but as if in foolishness, in this matter of boasting.
Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast.
For you gladly put up with fools, being wise yourselves.
For you put up with it if someone enslaves you, if someone devours you, if someone takes from you, if someone exalts himself over you, if someone strikes you in the face.
I say it to your shame that we were weak, as it were. But whatever anyone dares to boast of (I am speaking in foolishness), I too will dare.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.
Are they servants of Christ? I am speaking even more foolishly: I am more so. I have had far more labours, far more sufferings, imprisonments beyond measure, and I have often faced death.
Five times I received from the Jews forty lashes minus one.
Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked, and I spent a night and a day in the deep.

I have been on frequent journeys, in dangers from rivers, dangers from robbers, dangers from the Gentiles, dangers in cities, dangers in the wilderness, dangers at sea, and dangers from false brothers,
in labour and toil, often without sleep, in hunger and thirst, often fasting, in cold and nakedness.
Besides all that, there is what comes upon me day after day: concern for all the churches.
Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is made to stumble, and I do not burn?
If boasting is necessary, I will boast of my weakness.
The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying.
In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas had surrounded the city of the Damascenes and wanted to seize me;
And I was let down through a window in a basket over the wall, and escaped from his hands.
If boasting is necessary, it is not fitting; but I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago (whether in the body or without the body, I do not know; God knows) was caught up, such a man, as far as the third heaven.
And I know that such a man (whether in the body or without the body, I do not know; God knows)
was caught up into paradise and heard that unspeakable word which it is not permitted for men to speak.
Of such a one I will boast; but of myself I will not boast, except in my weaknesses.
If I should wish to boast, I would not be foolish, for I am speaking the truth; but I refrain, lest anyone should think of me more than what he sees in me or hears from me.
Because of this surpassing revelation, so that I would not exalt myself, a thorn in the flesh was given to me: an assailing angel, to torment me, so that I would not exalt myself.
Concerning this I besought the Lord three times that he would remove it from me.
And he said to me: "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness." Therefore I will most gladly rather boast in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
Therefore I am content in my weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake; for when I am weak, then I am strong.
I have become foolish, because you compelled me. It was fitting that you should have borne witness for me, for in nothing was I inferior to the very great apostles, even though I am nothing.
For the signs of an apostle were performed among you with all patience, with signs and wonders and mighty works.
Now what is it in which you were made less than the other churches, except that I did not burden you in anything? Forgive me this wrong.

Behold, for the third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not burden you, for I do not want anything of yours, but you. For it is not the children who lay up treasure for the parents, but the parents for the children.
And I will gladly spend and be utterly spent for your souls; though the more I love you, the less I am loved.
But I did not burden you in anything; yet I was crafty and caught you by guile.
Did I take advantage of you in anything through any of those whom I sent to you?
I urged Titus, and sent the brother with him. Did Titus take advantage of you in anything? Did we not walk in the same spirit? Did we not follow in the same steps?
Again, you may think that we are making our defence to you. We speak before God in Christ; and all things, beloved, are for your edification.

For I fear that perhaps when I come I may not find you as I wish, and that I may be found by you as you do not wish; that perhaps there may be quarrelling and envy, outbursts of anger, factions, evil schemings, whisperings, arrogance, disorders.

I fear that perhaps, when I come, my God may humble me again before you, and I may mourn over many of those who sinned before and have not repented of the impurity, fornication and lewdness that they committed.
Behold, this is the third time I am coming to you. By the mouth of two or three witnesses every word shall be established.
I said it before, and now I say it again in advance, as I did when I was present then, and now while absent: to those who sinned before and to all the others, if I come again, I will not spare you.
Or are you seeking proof of the one who speaks through me, Christ? He is not weak toward you but is powerful among you.
For even though he was crucified in weakness, yet he lives by the power of God. And we too are weak toward him, but we shall live with him by the power of God, together with you.
Test yourselves, whether you are in the faith. Examine yourselves. Or do you not know for yourselves that Christ is among you? Unless you are somehow unproven.
For we hope that you will know that we are not unproven.
And we pray to God that you may do no evil at all. This is not so that we may appear proven, but so that you may do good, even if we are as though unproven.
For we have no power to speak anything evil against the truth, but only on the side of the truth.
We rejoice when we are weak and you are strong. This also I pray for: your steadfastness.
For this reason I write these things while absent, so that when I come I may not have to act unsparingly with the authority which the Lord gave me for building up and not for tearing down.
From now on, brothers, rejoice, be steadfast, be comforted, be of one mind, live in peace; and the God of peace and love will be with you.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all. Amen.
